title: Transaction ID Wraparound and Freezing
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main terms of Transaction ID Wraparound and Freezing.
Use or interpret an appropriate PostgreSQL example connected to transaction id age.
Identify one edge case and select a safe way to verify the expected result.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on Transaction ID Wraparound and Freezing. Its primary job is to help you operate a PostgreSQL instance by reading evidence from settings, logs, statistics, vacuum and storage tools. The listed PDF subtopics define the coverage expected here; work through them in order and connect each one to an example, edge case and checkable result.
content.why_it_matters: This topic matters because PostgreSQL systems must preserve correct results as data grows and more sessions or services interact with it. Practicing transaction id wraparound and freezing teaches you to make assumptions explicit, apply the right SQL or operational tool, and verify behavior instead of relying on a demonstration that only worked once.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep the problem small: operate a PostgreSQL instance by reading evidence from settings, logs, statistics, vacuum and storage tools. A PostgreSQL feature should be chosen for the semantics it provides, not just because it is available. Before executing a change, state the inputs, expected output and boundary conditions. The example below is intentionally small enough to inspect; it illustrates the idea but is not a substitute for a test against your schema and PostgreSQL version.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Transaction ID Wraparound and Freezing
content_blocks.expected_output: Both SELECTs return their values; the savepoint demonstrates returning to an earlier transaction point. No data is modified.
content_blocks.safety_note: The example is non-mutating, but the same control flow applies to data-changing statements.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Execute the block in a scratch session that supports explicit transactions.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For a read-only SELECT or inspection command, no reset is needed. For DDL/DML, use a disposable database; capture the starting state, run the example, inspect the result, and ROLLBACK or drop the lab objects as appropriate. Do not use production data or credentials.

task: Create a short practice artifact for “Transaction ID Wraparound and Freezing”: explain its goal, show one example linked to “Transaction ID age”, state the expected result, and include one edge/failure case and verification method. Use a disposable database or static artifact as appropriate.
hints: Start with the listed subtopics, especially “Transaction ID age”, and describe the expected behavior in your own words.
Run or inspect the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior; do not add unrelated features before it is verified.
When the result surprises you, capture the exact SQL/error, check version and permissions, and change one assumption at a time.
expected_output: A reviewable note or query for Transaction ID Wraparound and Freezing, with an explanation of “Transaction ID age”, expected behavior, and a documented edge-case check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying the example without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Object names, data types, privileges, extensions and data distribution affect database behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: List schema/version assumptions and test with a tiny synthetic dataset first.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a single successful query as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: A happy-path result does not test invalid input, concurrent sessions, permissions, recovery or query performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one negative/edge case and record the evidence that confirms the expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Making a production change directly from a lesson.
common_mistakes.why: DDL, data updates, role changes and operational commands can affect data or availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use an isolated lab, reviewed migration, least privilege, rollback/recovery plan and a second-person review for production.

summary: Transaction ID Wraparound and Freezing fits into the broader goal to operate a PostgreSQL instance by reading evidence from settings, logs, statistics, vacuum and storage tools.
